quizName: DMV Practice Test #8 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When stopping, you should:
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. This helps you brake quickly and safely.

questions.question: How should you brake?
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: When starting your motorcycle, the engine should be in:
questions.explanation: Put your motorcycle in neutral before you start the engine. Most motorcycles have a light on the speedometer that shows when the bike is in neutral.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection:

options.text: Should only be done by a certified mechanic.

questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. This inspection takes only a few minutes.

questions.question: When buying a motorcycle helmet, you should be most concerned about the helmet's:
questions.explanation: Protection should be your main concern when choosing a motorcycle helmet.

questions.question: If riding during the day, you should wear:
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear clothing with reflective material to be more visible, even in daylight. Always wear clothing that covers your arms and legs.

questions.question: If you have a passenger aboard your motorcycle, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Ride at speeds that are slower than usual.
Allow more distance to stop than usual.
Tell the passenger to hold onto the back of the bike.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the passenger to hold onto the back of the bike.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight, so your motorcycle will handle differently. Ride slower and give yourself more time to stop. Your passenger should hold onto the handgrips or your waist, not the back of the bike.

questions.question: When entering a turn, it is best to:

options.text: Take the motorcycle out of gear.

questions.explanation: Change gears before you enter a turn. If you must change gears while turning, do so slowly and smoothly.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.
Only stop to yield to other traffic.
Vehicles will be entering the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. Stop completely, let other traffic and pedestrians pass, and then go when it is safe.

questions.question: You are most likely to get into a collision:
questions.explanation: Intersections are where you are most likely to collide with other traffic.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright, reflective clothing whenever you ride, day or night.

questions.question: The front brake provides about how much of a motorcycle's stopping power?
questions.explanation: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of your motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: Why should you change gears before starting a turn?

options.text: To prevent a sudden change in power during the turn.
To keep both hands on the handle grips during the turn.
To keep the motorcycle from slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: To prevent a sudden change in power during the turn.
questions.explanation: Change gears before you start a turn. Shifting during a turn can cause a sudden change in power to the rear wheel and cause a skid. If you must shift during a turn, do it smoothly.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell you about traffic laws in that area. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, what should you turn?
questions.explanation: Look through a turn by turning only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: If you and another vehicle reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, what should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlight so the other vehicle knows to proceed.
Continue through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no signs or traffic lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign is on the back of slow-moving vehicles that go slower than 25 mph. Examples include farm equipment, construction machinery, and horse-drawn vehicles.

questions.question: What should you do if a tailgater is following you?

options.text: Change lanes to let them pass or slow down to create more space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes to let them pass or slow down to create more space.
questions.explanation: Encourage a tailgater to pass by changing lanes or slowing down. Speeding up may only make them tailgate you at higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that a railroad crossing is coming.

questions.question: Smaller vehicles appear to be ________ and slower than they really are.
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge the speed and distance of small vehicles like motorcycles. Do not assume that drivers of larger vehicles can accurately judge your speed and location.

questions.question: How should you position yourself to properly control a motorcycle?

options.text: Let your feet hang off the footrests.
Use your arms to hold up your body.
Keep your knees against the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank.
questions.explanation: Keep your knees against the gas tank to help balance during turns. Bend your arms slightly and use them to steer, not to support your weight. This position lets you control all the motorcycle's controls easily.

questions.question: What should a rider's boots or shoes do?

options.text: Be made of soft, flexible material.

questions.explanation: Wear sturdy boots or shoes that cover and support your ankles. The soles should be hard, slip-resistant, and durable.

questions.question: Which is NOT a reason to keep space between your motorcycle and the vehicle ahead?

options.text: It gives you more time to react to hazards.
It prevents you from finding an escape route.
It gives you space to steer your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It prevents you from finding an escape route.
questions.explanation: Space between vehicles helps you react if another driver makes a mistake. It also gives you room to safely steer your motorcycle. Having this space is beneficial, not harmful.

questions.question: Which is NOT a way to stay in control during a motorcycle turn?
questions.explanation: Slow down before you turn. Look ahead in the direction you want to go. Lean the motorcycle in the right direction. Gently roll on the throttle through the turn to keep the suspension stable.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop quickly?

options.text: Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, press both the front and rear brakes at the same time with controlled pressure.
